source: Dune · How to play, Luis Civolani
version: Page identifies Gale Force Nine 2019 rules rewritten for study. No page revision date or version was displayed.
access: Research browser/direct retrieval returned HTTP 403. The normal in-app browser loaded successfully; reading used CUA UI controls and accessibility state only.

otherSections: Discovery token procedures and all eight token descriptions
All base Treachery Card descriptions exposed by accessibility state
excluded: Interactive quiz and simulator outcomes: not required for reading, not used as validation oracles

observations.text: Mode controls replace ordinary section text, phase tabs teach one step at a time, and faction sheets separate abilities, ally gifts and special Karama. Useful examples of accessible progressive teaching.

observations.guide: Any number of cards up to the whole hand.
observations.decision: Retain up-to-four decision GF9-CORE-013; the teaching summary does not override collected quantitative evidence.

observations.guide: Faction summary says Karama cards can only block.
observations.decision: Do not adopt this shorthand. Ordinary Karama bidding and shipment uses remain available; absence of a faction special power is a separate rule.

observations.guide: Short summaries describe ambassadors triggering when another faction walks in, and Moritani gaining Vidal after two stronghold battles, without every qualification.
observations.decision: Retain complete expansion conditions. Summaries do not establish new timing or trigger exceptions.

observations.guide: Ally gift says to ship the ally with a No-Field token.
observations.decision: Retain the exact printed ally-shipment procedure in the authored expansion rules; do not import ambiguous paraphrase.

observations.guide: Basic explanation says one new ally must move out and describes a fallback for the second mover.
observations.decision: Retain the official clarified later-player evacuation procedure and explicit Ecaz exception recorded in GF9-CORE-005.

observations.guide: Advanced spice panel says every worm after the first may be moved, without specifying consecutiveness in that short line.
observations.decision: Retain the source-backed consecutive-worm condition; no new freedom is inferred from a summary.

observations.guide: Pile A can cause a Nexus before pile B, and pile B can cause another.
observations.decision: Consistent with the corrected specific Advanced sequence in GF9-CORE-016; no further change.

observations.guide: Hajr and Family Atomics are described briefly, without every precise play restriction.
observations.decision: Keep the detailed ordinary rules and card timing already authored from the source corpus.

followup: No new official-source contradiction found. Existing judgements cover the overlapping disagreements; further omissions are teaching shorthand, not rules to adopt.
